title: Demonstrate understanding of rational and irrational numbers and number systems

lessons.title: Kinds of numbers
lessons.html:
The family of numbers

We use numbers every day at work: counting carcasses, weighing meat, measuring temperature. Numbers belong to different groups.

GroupWhat they areExamples
Natural numbersCounting numbers1, 2, 3, 4 ...
Whole numbersNatural numbers and zero0, 1, 2, 3 ...
IntegersWhole numbers and their negatives... −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 ...
Rational numbersNumbers that can be written as a fraction a/b, where b is not 01/2, −3/4, 0.25, 5
Irrational numbersNumbers that cannot be written as a fractionπ (pi), √2, √3
Real numbersAll rational and irrational numbers togetherAll of the above

Negative numbers at work

Freezers run below zero. If a freezer is at −18 °C and a chiller is at 4 °C, the difference is 4 − (−18) = 22 degrees.

Rational numbers as decimals

  • Some fractions give a decimal that stops: 1/4 = 0.25, 3/8 = 0.375. These are terminating decimals.
  • Some fractions give a decimal that repeats: 1/3 = 0.333..., 2/11 = 0.1818... These are recurring decimals.
  • Both kinds are rational.

Irrational numbers

An irrational number has a decimal that never stops and never repeats. π = 3.14159... is used to work out the area and edge of circles, such as round tanks. √2 = 1.41421... We round irrational numbers when we use them, for example π ≈ 3.14.

Every natural number is also a whole number.

Every integer is also a rational number.

lessons.title: Working with fractions, decimals and percentages
lessons.html:
Changing between forms

The same amount can be written as a fraction, a decimal or a percentage.

FractionDecimalPercentage
1/20.550%
1/40.2525%
3/40.7575%
1/100.110%
  • Fraction to decimal: divide the top by the bottom. 3/5 = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.
  • Decimal to percentage: multiply by 100. 0.6 × 100 = 60%.
  • Percentage to decimal: divide by 100. 15% = 0.15.

Example at work

A carcass weighs 250 kg. The trimmings are 1/50 of the weight. 250 ÷ 50 = 5 kg. As a percentage: 1/50 = 0.02 = 2%.

Rounding

To round to one decimal place, look at the second decimal. If it is 5 or more, round up. 12.46 kg becomes 12.5 kg. 12.43 kg becomes 12.4 kg.

Estimating

Before you calculate, estimate. 19 crates × 21 kg is about 20 × 20 = 400 kg. The exact answer is 399 kg. If your calculator showed 3 990, you would know something was wrong.

Ratios

Cleaning chemicals are often mixed as a ratio, for example 1 : 100, which means 1 part chemical to 100 parts water. For 10 litres of water you need 10 ÷ 100 = 0.1 litre, which is 100 ml of chemical. Always follow the label.

Always write the unit with your answer, such as kg, litres or %. A number without a unit can be misread and cause mistakes at work.

Check your answers with a calculator.

lessons.title: Large and small numbers and number systems
lessons.html:
Powers of ten

Big and small numbers are easier to write with powers of ten.

  • 10² = 10 × 10 = 100
  • 10³ = 1 000
  • 10⁶ = 1 000 000 (one million)

Scientific notation writes a number as a number between 1 and 10 times a power of ten.

  • 45 000 = 4.5 × 10⁴
  • 3 200 000 = 3.2 × 10⁶
  • 0.003 = 3 × 10⁻³

A laboratory may report that a swab had 2 × 10³ bacteria. That is 2 000 bacteria.

Units and prefixes

PrefixMeaningExample
kilo (k)× 1 0001 kg = 1 000 g
milli (m)÷ 1 0001 ml = 0.001 litre
centi (c)÷ 1001 cm = 0.01 m

Number systems

We normally use the decimal system (base 10). It has ten digits, 0 to 9. Each place is worth ten times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands.

Computers use the binary system (base 2). It has only two digits, 0 and 1. Each place is worth two times the place to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 ...

  • Binary 101 = (1 × 4) + (0 × 2) + (1 × 1) = 5.
  • Binary 1101 = 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13.

Time uses yet another system: 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour.

Key points

  • Rational numbers can be written as fractions; irrational numbers like π and √2 cannot.
  • Terminating and recurring decimals are both rational.
  • Change between fractions, decimals and percentages by dividing or multiplying by 100.
  • Estimate first to check your answer.
  • Scientific notation and powers of ten make big and small numbers easy to write.
